doc.title: Plas Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

chapter: Opening and arrival in Los Angeles
title: First steady job in Long Beach with George Jenkins
summary: A six-nights-a-week sailor-town job in Long Beach with drummer George Jenkins, Wesley Prince and his brother, after jam sessions for a few dollars.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well I didn’t start playing rhythm & blues, I started playing anywhere I could get a job, but actually one of my first jobs really was a jazz job, kind of a jazz job in the city of Long Beach, with a drummer called George Jenkins, who was Dinah Washington’s first husband, and played with Lionel Hampton and he was a great drummer. Let’s see, me, George, Wesley Prince and my brother on piano, we played in a joint out in Long Beach which was kind of a sailor town with bars and music six nights a week. And stayed there. We stayed there for about six months. So that was our first big job where we had a steady job. Before that we were doing jam sessions for three dollars. Five dollars.
I guess they call that scuffling, huh?

Paying your dues, all those things. Sounds like you have to do it I guess. I’m going to test your memory now, can you tell me some of the first solos that you did on some of these recordings that went on to sell some records?
